title: Convex geometry and the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv problem: Theorem 1.2
abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of Theorem 1.2 of Dmitrii Zakharov's Convex geometry and the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv problem. For every fixed positive dimension d, as p tends to infinity through the primes, the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant s(F_p^d) satisfies s(F_p^d) = p w(F_p^d) + o(p), where w is the weak Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant.  Supporting proofs include the convex-flag Helly and centerpoint theorems, flag decomposition lemma, balanced convex combinations, relative set expansion, and the polynomial method bound for w. This submission covers Theorem 1.2 and its upper-bound formulation, not every result in the paper. The submission was prepared with the assistance of ChatGPT 5.6 / 6 Sol-Ultra under the direction and review of the author.  The GitHub page includes a PDF file zakharov_2026-3.pdf containing a revised version of the published paper generated  by ChatGPT 5.6 during this formalization project.  The only noteworthy difference is a correction to Definition 4.6 (Proper points) which was meant to use the function f^circ(q) in  place of \hat f(q) in the published version (this typo slipped in during one of the revision rounds of the paper). No other significant mistakes or corrections were discovered.
